# Skill: present-interactive-analysis
Skill directory (use as SKILL_ROOT): D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\opal-work\clio-agent-chart-guidance\src\clio_agent\gact\builtin_skills\present-interactive-analysis
Use this generic presentation skill only after the underlying evidence exists and
only when interaction or structure helps the user more than prose. A2UI is a view
of observed state, never an analysis substitute. Do not mention the protocol or
ask the user to supply component payloads.

Component shapes are NOT in this skill — the catalog itself is the allowlist and
the source of truth (`docs/design/a2ui-compat-campaign-2026-09.md` S2/S4). Load a
catalog's index with `load_skill("a2ui-catalog-<slug>")` (see "Skills available to
you" for the ids your session can currently produce) and one component's exact
schema with `load_skill("a2ui-catalog-<slug>", file="catalog.json#/components/<Name>")`
before producing it.

## Choosing a view

Match the surface to the shape of the evidence, not to what looks impressive:

- A spatial result (stations, sites, points on a map) → a map component.
- Structured rows and columns → a data table.
- A quantity that changes over an index or time for a few series → an interactive
  time series.
- Many entities or grouped comparisons (one line per sample over time, spectra,
  distributions per group, a matrix of values) → the catalog's general chart
  component. Use one of its **named presets** by filling in field names; don't
  write a chart spec by hand unless no preset fits. That's longer, more likely to
  fail, and still has to pass the catalog's spec guard.
- For anything non-trivial in size, pass a registered artifact reference instead
  of inlined rows. Let the server-side query filter, aggregate or downsample it
  (for example, a bounded number of points per entity) instead of trimming the
  data yourself.
- A single observed value → one metric component per value.
- Ongoing/completed work, a warning, or a diff → the matching status/callout/diff
  component, never repurposing a generic text block for it.
- A durable export (an image, a report) the user did not ask to view inline → a
  registered artifact reference, not an inlined image.

## Composing surfaces

Prefer one small surface at the step it explains. Reuse a stable semantic
`surface_id` to update that view in place. Do not accumulate unrelated work into
one final tabbed dashboard. Tabs are appropriate only when several views of the
same result belong together and the available width justifies them.

## Custom charts with Altair

The general chart component renders **Vega-Lite**. When no named preset fits
(a layered overlay, a particular facet layout, a custom encoding), write the
chart in Python with **Altair**, which produces Vega-Lite, and pass the
exported spec to the component instead of writing Vega-Lite JSON by hand.

- **Data comes only from the component.** Build every chart on
  `alt.NamedData("source")`. A DataFrame, URL or inline values passed to
  `alt.Chart(...)` get inlined into the spec, and the server's chart guard
  refuses them. Rows arrive through the component's inline data or its
  artifact reference.
- **Shared selection.** Define one point selection whose name matches the
  component's selection parameter, over the entity field. The component's
  selection binding then links the chart to the other views (see below).
- **Keep specs small.** The guard caps size, nesting and view count. No URLs
  anywhere.

Write a Python file that assigns the Altair chart to `chart`, resolve this
skill's directory as `SKILL_ROOT`, and export plus pre-check it:

```text
uv run --no-project --with "altair>=5" python "SKILL_ROOT/scripts/vega_spec.py" build "CHART.py" "SPEC.json"
```

The script writes the spec and names any rule it would obviously break;
`vega_spec.py check SPEC.json` re-checks an existing spec. The server's guard
is the final authority. Load the chart component's schema from the catalog
skill before putting the spec into a surface.

## Linking views on one surface

To let several views on the same surface follow one selection, bind each view's
selection to the same data-model path under `/selection/`, one path per concept
(e.g. the selected samples). A chart, table or map on that surface then
highlights whatever the others select, entirely in the client, with no agent
turn. Use this whenever views show the same entities from different angles.
Views on different surfaces don't share selection.

## Preserving a user's choice into the next turn

A click or selection inside a surface is local visual state only — it does not by
itself reach the agent. When the user must choose among options before analysis
continues, pair the selector with a submit action whose event delivers the
resolved selection as structured context; load the catalog's Button/action and
your chosen selector's schemas together so the wiring between them is correct on
the first try.

## Producing and verifying

Call `create_a2ui_surface` once per coherent revision (leave `catalog_id` empty
to use the session's negotiated catalog). Require `rendered=true` and
`state=ready` before saying the view is available. A refusal names what to load
next (`hint`) — load exactly that component's schema, correct the call, and
retry a bounded number of times; do not print the payload as chat text, silently
replace an interactive component with a static image, or claim success on a
refusal.

Bundled files (load with load_skill(skill_id, file=...)):
- scripts/vega_spec.py

# Experiment card

Facts about this one dataset. Tag every line: `[stated]` (the export says so;
cite the file), `[checked]` (verified in the data; cite the command or
script output), `[inferred]` (an interpretation; list it under open questions
until the data owners confirm it). Never copy a fact from another dataset's card.

## Identity

- [checked] bundle root when the card was created: `D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\OPAL\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC`
- [checked] manifest `manifest.json` sha256 `76bf90275f7a98392fc6d1363b46cc3a28142ebfd219c8705e19636604771757`
- [stated] export_version: 6
- [stated] generated_at: 2026-09-02T08:25:02+00:00

## Stated facts

- [stated] This is experiment 67, `2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC`, generated on 2026-09-02 with export_version 6. (source: `manifest.json`, `experiment`, `generated_at`, `export_version`)
- [stated] The manifest declares FC1, RGB2, MSC1, VNIR, SWIR, and S3D modality tables, plus top-level plant weights. (source: `manifest.json`, `modalities` and `top_level_files`)
- [stated] Feature, metadata, and design tables within a modality join on `sample_key`; asset paths are relative to the export root. (source: `README.md`, “How To Use This Export”)
- [stated] RGB2 is top-view projected imaging; VNIR and SWIR signatures are masked median reflectance by wavelength; FC1 includes vendor plant scalars and parameter-image masked medians. (source: `docs/experiment-export-summary.md`, “Modality Status” and “Feature Families”; YAML blocks in `docs/modalities/RGB2.md`, `VNIR.md`, `SWIR.md`, and `FC1.md`)
- [stated] The FC1 variable catalog labels `Size` as `mm2` and its other 199 variables as `a.u.`; S3D supplies canonical traits and units separately from vendor units. (source: `fc1/fc1-variables.parquet`, `s3d/s3d-variables.parquet`)
- [stated] The generated README reports zero data issues and lists FC2, RGB1, ROOT, IR1, and MSC2 as requested modalities without feature rows. (source: `README.md`, “Requested Modalities With No Feature Rows”; `manifest.json`, `data_issues_count`)

## Checked facts

- [checked] The manifest SHA-256 matches this card; all 27 manifest-declared Parquet row counts matched file metadata; the inventory found no missing manifest references or unreferenced tables. (evidence: `card.py status`, direct PyArrow Parquet metadata check, `audit/inventory.json`)
- [checked] The design has 360 plants. RGB2 has 12 genotype labels and six treatment labels (`0`, `50`, `100`, `200`, `500`, `1000`), with five plants in every genotype–treatment cell; repeated factor values showed no within- or cross-modality conflicts. (evidence: full design-table PyArrow check)
- [checked] Plant coverage is FC1 360, RGB2 360, MSC1 360, VNIR 353, SWIR 360, and S3D 359. Round counts are respectively 48, 67, 67, 23, 23, and 22. (evidence: full design-table PyArrow check)
- [checked] The 14 feature–metadata/design/signature `sample_key` joins were one-to-one with no unmatched rows. FC1 and S3D long tables matched all feature samples on `experiment_id,plant_id,round_id`; joins on their raw `sample_key` or case-sensitive S3D modality would not match. (evidence: `audit/join-*.json`)
- [checked] FC1 values contain 328,740 float-maximum values with empty QC flags. Another 203,394 FC1 values are null and correctly flagged `no_finite_masked_pixels`. (evidence: `audit/columns-fc1-fc1_values.json`, `audit/flags-fc1-values.json`, full Parquet scan)
- [checked] VNIR and SWIR signature tables contain respectively 473 and 634 all-empty string-typed band columns alongside populated numeric bands with near-duplicate wavelength labels. The populated bands have unique wavelengths. (evidence: `audit/columns-vnir-signatures.json`, `audit/columns-swir-signatures.json`, populated-band check)
- [checked] In FC1, RGB2, VNIR, and SWIR, all roundness values above 1e6 coincide with zero perimeter; no such extreme occurs with nonzero perimeter. (evidence: full feature-table PyArrow check)
- [checked] The plant-weights table has 25,752 distinct non-null `sample_key` values, including 12 plant–timestamp pairs with two different weight readings. Seven rows contain at least one zero weight. (evidence: DuckDB key check and full `plant-weights.parquet` inspection)
- [checked] Round metadata includes `Warning` and `UserTerminated` statuses, and some rounds contain fewer plants than the sensor’s maximum. FC1, RGB2, and MSC1 also have multiple observations for some plant-day pairs. (evidence: full metadata-table PyArrow checks)
- [checked] The loader generated 360 design rows, 5,431,833 observation rows in 40 chunks, 191,567 asset rows, 25,819 event rows, and 35 bounded spectra chunks. Design, assets, events, all 40 observation chunks, and all 35 spectra chunks passed schema validation. A combined DuckDB check across the observation chunks found no missing required fields, float-maximum sentinels, or duplicate observation keys. (evidence: loader output, `audit/view-validation-*.json`, combined observations DuckDB check)

## Inferred facts

- [inferred] Numeric-looking treatment labels may represent doses, but neither treatment identity nor dose unit is established here; they remain categorical strings with null numeric dose fields. (why: six numeric-looking labels in design; confirm with: experiment owners)
- [inferred] The exported imaging timestamps lack an explicit timezone; the loader preserves them without adding an offset. (why: source timestamp examples and Parquet schemas; confirm with: APPL team)
- [inferred] FC1 float-maximum values are nonmeasurements rather than biological readings; the loader nulls them and marks `sentinel_float_max`. (why: exact float64 maximum repeated 328,740 times with no QC flag; confirm with: APPL team)

## Traps found

- [trap:sentinel-values] `fc1/fc1-values.parquet:value` -- 328,740 float64-maximum values are unflagged -- loader writes null and `sentinel_float_max`; raw file is unchanged. (evidence: full column audit and Parquet scan)
- [trap:unflagged-missing] FC1 vendor scalar QC -- float-maximum nonmeasurements have empty `qc_flags`, although explicit null masked medians carry `no_finite_masked_pixels` -- loader checks the value itself rather than trusting flags alone. (evidence: `audit/flags-fc1-values.json` and full Parquet scan)
- [trap:ghost-columns] VNIR/SWIR signatures -- 473/634 string-typed band columns are all empty -- loader unpivots only populated numeric bands. (evidence: signature column audits)
- [trap:near-duplicate-columns] VNIR/SWIR signatures -- empty and populated wavelength names differ slightly by rounding -- loader retains populated numeric names and parses their wavelength labels without merging bands. (evidence: signature column audits)
- [trap:ghost-columns] modality design and feature tables -- `design_plant_id` and several modality-inapplicable asset fields are empty -- loader uses populated canonical factors and asset paths only. (evidence: `audit/columns-*-design.json`, feature column audits)
- [trap:key-format-mismatch] FC1/S3D long measurements -- raw `sample_key` suffixes/case and S3D modality capitalization differ from feature tables -- loader associates measurement rows using `experiment_id,plant_id,round_id`, preserving original source keys for traceability. (evidence: `audit/join-*-components.json` and failed raw-key overlap audits)
- [trap:design-encoding] design treatment fields -- treatment labels look numeric and duplicate `design_spike`/`design_treatment_1`, but no dose unit is established -- loader keeps canonical `treatment` as a string and leaves `treatment_value`/`treatment_unit` null. (evidence: design column audits and full factor check)
- [trap:impossible-values] FC1/RGB2/VNIR/SWIR derived roundness -- zero perimeter produces extreme roundness -- loader nulls only derived roundness where its corresponding perimeter is zero; area and perimeter remain unchanged. (evidence: full feature-table PyArrow check)
- [trap:irregular-sampling] modality metadata -- partial rounds, warning/terminated statuses, and repeated plant-day observations occur -- loader preserves exact timestamps, round IDs, statuses, and all observations; it does not silently select a daily session. (evidence: full metadata checks)
- [trap:duplicate-measures] FC1 values -- vendor plant scalar and masked parameter-image median can measure the same named variable -- loader gives them separate methods and does not choose one. (evidence: `fc1/fc1-values.parquet` source/aggregation checks)
- [trap:duplicate-measures] plant weights -- 12 plant–timestamp groups have distinct readings -- loader preserves both with source weight IDs in `method` and original `sample_key`. (evidence: full `plant-weights.parquet` key check)
- [trap:impossible-values] plant weights -- seven rows have at least one zero whose meaning is undocumented -- loader preserves zero and marks `zero_weight_unresolved`. (evidence: full `plant-weights.parquet` inspection)
- [trap:sentinel-values] FC1 and feature tables -- isolated `-99`, `9999`, and `32767` values are sentinel candidates but not confirmed -- loader retains them with `possible_sentinel_code` rather than silently nulling them. (evidence: column audit reports and FC1 value scan)
- [trap:unit-scale-suspect] S3D variables -- vendor unit is `a.u.` while exported canonical traits use `mm`, `mm2`, `mm3`, ratios, or counts -- loader uses exported canonical traits/units without converting values; calibration remains unconfirmed. (evidence: `s3d/s3d-variables.parquet` and long values)
- [trap:declared-vs-actual] `data-issues` count -- the export declares zero issues, yet independent audits found missing and suspect measurements -- loader does not treat the empty issue log as proof of clean data. (evidence: `manifest.json:data_issues_count`, column and flag audits)

## Open questions for data owners

- What substance or intervention do treatment labels `0`, `50`, `100`, `200`, `500`, and `1000` represent, and are they doses with a unit? This determines whether dose-response analysis is valid.
- What timezone, if any, applies to image, round, and weighing timestamps? This affects cross-sensor timing and daily aggregation.
- Are FC1 float64-maximum values vendor missing-value codes, and should `-99`/`9999` and feature-table `32767` also be treated as missing? This changes trait summaries.
- Are zero pre- or post-watering weights genuine observations or failed readings? This changes water/weight analyses.
- Which of the duplicate weight readings at the same plant and timestamp should be authoritative, if either? This changes longitudinal weight summaries.
- For FC1 variables available as both vendor scalars and masked parameter-image medians, which method is intended for each scientific comparison? This changes fluorescence results.
- Are S3D canonical metric units calibrated and comparable to other sensors, given the `a.u.` vendor-unit fields? This changes cross-sensor size comparisons.
- Should `Warning` and `UserTerminated` rounds be excluded, and how should multiple same-day sessions be selected or aggregated? This changes time-course analyses.

## Traps found

- [trap:sentinel-values] `fc1/fc1-values.parquet:value` -- 328,740 float64-maximum values are unflagged -- loader writes null and `sentinel_float_max`; raw file is unchanged. (evidence: full column audit and Parquet scan)
- [trap:unflagged-missing] FC1 vendor scalar QC -- float-maximum nonmeasurements have empty `qc_flags`, although explicit null masked medians carry `no_finite_masked_pixels` -- loader checks the value itself rather than trusting flags alone. (evidence: `audit/flags-fc1-values.json` and full Parquet scan)
- [trap:ghost-columns] VNIR/SWIR signatures -- 473/634 string-typed band columns are all empty -- loader unpivots only populated numeric bands. (evidence: signature column audits)
- [trap:near-duplicate-columns] VNIR/SWIR signatures -- empty and populated wavelength names differ slightly by rounding -- loader retains populated numeric names and parses their wavelength labels without merging bands. (evidence: signature column audits)

(evidence: `audit/join-*-components.json` and failed raw-key overlap audits)
- [trap:design-encoding] design treatment fields -- treatment labels look numeric and duplicate `design_spike`/`design_treatment_1`, but no dose unit is established -- loader keeps canonical `treatment` as a string and leaves `treatment_value`/`treatment_unit` null. (evidence: design column audits and full factor check)
- [trap:impossible-values] FC1/RGB2/VNIR/SWIR derived roundness -- zero perimeter produces extreme roundness -- loader nulls only derived roundness where its corresponding perimeter is zero; area and perimeter remain unchanged. (evidence: full feature-table PyArrow check)
- [trap:irregular-sampling] modality metadata -- partial rounds, warning/terminated statuses, and repeated plant-day observations occur -- loader preserves exact timestamps, round IDs, statuses, and all observations; it does not silently select a daily session. (evidence: full metadata checks)
- [trap:duplicate-measures] FC1 values -- vendor plant scalar and masked parameter-image median can measure the same named variable -- loader gives them separate methods and does not choose one. (evidence: `fc1/fc1-values.parquet` source/aggregation checks)
- [trap:duplicate-measures] plant weights -- 12 plant–timestamp groups have distinct readings -- loader preserves both with source weight IDs in `method` and original `sample_key`. (evidence: full `plant-weights.parquet` key check)
- [trap:impossible-values] plant weights -- seven rows have at least one zero whose meaning is undocumented -- loader preserves zero and marks `zero_weight_unresolved`. (evidence: full `plant-weights.parquet` inspection)
- [trap:sentinel-values] FC1 and feature tables -- isolated `-99`, `9999`, and `32767` values are sentinel candidates but not confirmed -- loader retains them with `possible_sentinel_code` rather than silently nulling them. (evidence: column audit reports and FC1 value scan)

(evidence: `s3d/s3d-variables.parquet` and long values)
- [trap:declared-vs-actual] `data-issues` count -- the export declares zero issues, yet independent audits found missing and suspect measurements -- loader does not treat the empty issue log as proof of clean data. (evidence: `manifest.json:data_issues_count`, column and flag audits)

## Open questions for data owners

- What substance or intervention do treatment labels `0`, `50`, `100`, `200`, `500`, and `1000` represent, and are they doses with a unit? This determines whether dose-response analysis is valid.
- What timezone, if any, applies to image, round, and weighing timestamps? This affects cross-sensor timing and daily aggregation.
- Are FC1 float64-maximum values vendor missing-value codes, and should `-99`/`9999` and feature-table `32767` also be treated as missing? This changes trait summaries.
- Are zero pre- or post-watering weights genuine observations or failed readings? This changes water/weight analyses.
- Which of the duplicate weight readings at the same plant and timestamp should be authoritative, if either? This changes longitudinal weight summaries.
- For FC1 variables available as both vendor scalars and masked parameter-image medians, which method is intended for each scientific comparison? This changes fluorescence results.
- Are S3D canonical metric units calibrated and comparable to other sensors, given the `a.u.` vendor-unit fields? This changes cross-sensor size comparisons.
- Should `Warning` and `UserTerminated` rounds be excluded, and how should multiple same-day sessions be selected or aggregated? This changes time-course analyses.
- Are the VNIR/SWIR reflectance values radiometrically calibrated and comparable between sessions, and which wavelength calibration should be considered authoritative? This changes spectral interpretation.
- Are RGB/MSC/VNIR/SWIR feature-name suffixes and undocumented indices sufficient to assign physical scales? The loader uses conservative name-derived scales where a documented unit is absent; interpretation needs confirmation.

## Proposed lessons

- check: whether a source-specific long table uses a different key format from its companion feature table before joining.
- check: whether empty wavelength columns coexist with populated columns bearing slightly different calibrated wavelength labels.
- check: whether duplicate plant–timestamp measurements have distinct source measurement IDs and disagree in value.
- check: whether a derived shape index becomes extreme exactly when its denominator-like perimeter is zero.

## Traps found

- [trap:sentinel-values] `fc1/fc1-values.parquet:value` -- 328,740 float64-maximum values are unflagged -- loader writes null and `sentinel_float_max`; raw file is unchanged. (evidence: full column audit and Parquet scan)
- [trap:unflagged-missing] FC1 vendor scalar QC -- float-maximum nonmeasurements have empty `qc_flags`, although explicit null masked medians carry `no_finite_masked_pixels` -- loader checks the value itself rather than trusting flags alone. (evidence: `audit/flags-fc1-values.json` and full Parquet scan)
- [trap:ghost-columns] VNIR/SWIR signatures -- 473/634 string-typed band columns are all empty -- loader unpivots only populated numeric bands. (evidence: signature column audits)
- [trap:near-duplicate-columns] VNIR/SWIR signatures -- empty and populated wavelength names differ slightly by rounding -- loader retains populated numeric names and parses their wavelength labels without merging bands. (evidence: signature column audits)
- [trap:ghost-columns] modality design and feature tables -- `design_plant_id` and several modality-inapplicable asset fields are empty -- loader uses populated canonical factors and asset paths only. (evidence: `audit/columns-*-design.json`, feature column audits)
- [trap:key-format-mismatch] FC1/S3D long measurements -- raw `sample_key` suffixes/case and S3D modality capitalization differ from feature tables -- loader associates measurement rows using `experiment_id,plant_id,round_id`, preserving original source keys for traceability. (evidence: `audit/join-*-components.json` and failed raw-key overlap audits)
- [trap:design-encoding] design treatment fields -- treatment labels look numeric and duplicate `design_spike`/`design_treatment_1`, but no dose unit is established -- loader keeps canonical `treatment` as a string and leaves `treatment_value`/`treatment_unit` null. (evidence: design column audits and full factor check)
- [trap:impossible-values] FC1/RGB2/VNIR/SWIR derived roundness -- zero perimeter produces extreme roundness -- loader nulls only derived roundness where its corresponding perimeter is zero; area and perimeter remain unchanged. (evidence: full feature-table PyArrow check)
- [trap:irregular-sampling] modality metadata -- partial rounds, warning/terminated statuses, and repeated plant-day observations occur -- loader preserves exact timestamps, round IDs, statuses, and all observations; it does not silently select a daily session. (evidence: full metadata checks)
- [trap:duplicate-measures] FC1 values -- vendor plant scalar and masked parameter-image median can measure the same named variable -- loader gives them separate methods and does not choose one. (evidence: `fc1/fc1-values.parquet` source/aggregation checks)
- [trap:duplicate-measures] plant weights -- 12 plant–timestamp groups have distinct readings -- loader preserves both with source weight IDs in `method` and original `sample_key`. (evidence: full `plant-weights.parquet` key check)
- [trap:impossible-values] plant weights -- seven rows have at least one zero whose meaning is undocumented -- loader preserves zero and marks `zero_weight_unresolved`. (evidence: full `plant-weights.parquet` inspection)
- [trap:sentinel-values] FC1 and feature tables -- isolated `-99`, `9999`, and `32767` values are sentinel candidates but not confirmed -- loader retains them with `possible_sentinel_code` rather than silently nulling them. (evidence: column audit reports and FC1 value scan)
- [trap:unit-scale-suspect] S3D variables -- vendor unit is `a.u.` while exported canonical traits use `mm`, `mm2`, `mm3`, ratios, or counts -- loader uses exported canonical traits/units without converting values; calibration remains unconfirmed. (evidence: `s3d/s3d-variables.parquet` and long values)
- [trap:declared-vs-actual] `data-issues` count -- the export declares zero issues, yet independent audits found missing and suspect measurements -- loader does not treat the empty issue log as proof of clean data. (evidence: `manifest.json:data_issues_count`, column and flag audits)

## Open questions for data owners

- What substance or intervention do treatment labels `0`, `50`, `100`, `200`, `500`, and `1000` represent, and are they doses with a unit? This determines whether dose-response analysis is valid.
- What timezone, if any, applies to image, round, and weighing timestamps? This affects cross-sensor timing and daily aggregation.
- Are FC1 float64-maximum values vendor missing-value codes, and should `-99`/`9999` and feature-table `32767` also be treated as missing? This changes trait summaries.
- Are zero pre- or post-watering weights genuine observations or failed readings? This changes water/weight analyses.
- Which of the duplicate weight readings at the same plant and timestamp should be authoritative, if either? This changes longitudinal weight summaries.
- For FC1 variables available as both vendor scalars and masked parameter-image medians, which method is intended for each scientific comparison? This changes fluorescence results.
- Are S3D canonical metric units calibrated and comparable to other sensors, given the `a.u.` vendor-unit fields? This changes cross-sensor size comparisons.
- Should `Warning` and `UserTerminated` rounds be excluded, and how should multiple same-day sessions be selected or aggregated? This changes time-course analyses.
- Are the VNIR/SWIR reflectance values radiometrically calibrated and comparable between sessions, and which wavelength calibration should be considered authoritative? This changes spectral interpretation.
- Are RGB/MSC/VNIR/SWIR feature-name suffixes and undocumented indices sufficient to assign physical scales? The loader uses conservative name-derived scales where a documented unit is absent; interpretation needs confirmation.

## Proposed lessons

- check: whether a source-specific long table uses a different key format from its companion feature table before joining.
- check: whether empty wavelength columns coexist with populated columns bearing slightly different calibrated wavelength labels.
- check: whether duplicate plant–timestamp measurements have distinct source measurement IDs and disagree in value.
- check: whether a derived shape index becomes extreme exactly when its denominator-like perimeter is zero.

from pathlib import Path
from collections import Counter
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

workspace = Path(r'D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\opal-work\live\ws')
bundle = Path(r'D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\OPAL\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC')
views = workspace / '.clio' / 'datasets' / '76bf90275f7a9839' / 'views'

for label, path, columns in [
    ('design', views / 'design.parquet', ['unit_id', 'genotype', 'treatment']),
    ('rgb2_view', views / 'observations_rgb2_features_000.parquet', ['unit_id', 'time', 'trait', 'method', 'scale', 'value', 'qc', 'source_row_key']),
    ('rgb2_source', bundle / 'rgb2' / 'rgb2-features.parquet', ['sample_key', 'plant_id', 'date', 'datetime', 'area_px', 'qc_flags', 'tray_roi_crop_row_start_px', 'tray_roi_crop_row_stop_px', 'tray_roi_crop_col_start_px', 'tray_roi_crop_col_stop_px', 'feature_bbox_row_start_px', 'feature_bbox_row_stop_px', 'feature_bbox_col_start_px', 'feature_bbox_col_stop_px']),
]:
    table = pq.read_table(path, columns=columns)
    rows = table.slice(0, 3).to_pylist()
    print(label, 'rows=', table.num_rows)
    for row in rows:
        print(row)
    if label == 'rgb2_view':
        traits = Counter(zip(table.column('trait').to_pylist(), table.column('method').to_pylist(), table.column('scale').to_pylist()))
        print('traits=', sorted(traits.items()))
'@ | uv run --no-project --with pyarrow python -

@'
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

workspace = Path(r'D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\opal-work\live\ws')
bundle = Path(r'D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\OPAL\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC')
views = workspace / '.clio' / 'datasets' / '76bf90275f7a9839' / 'views'

observed = pq.read_table(
    views / 'observations_rgb2_features_000.parquet',
    columns=['unit_id', 'time', 'trait', 'value', 'source_row_key'],
).to_pandas()
observed = observed.loc[observed['trait'].eq('area_px')].copy()
source_columns = [
    'sample_key', 'date',
    'tray_roi_crop_row_start_px', 'tray_roi_crop_row_stop_px',
    'tray_roi_crop_col_start_px', 'tray_roi_crop_col_stop_px',
    'feature_bbox_row_start_px', 'feature_bbox_row_stop_px',
    'feature_bbox_col_start_px', 'feature_bbox_col_stop_px',
]
source = pq.read_table(bundle / 'rgb2' / 'rgb2-features.parquet', columns=source_columns).to_pandas()
design = pq.read_table(views / 'design.parquet', columns=['unit_id', 'treatment', 'genotype']).to_pandas()
joined = observed.merge(source, left_on='source_row_key', right_on='sample_key', how='left', validate='one_to_one')
joined = joined.merge(design, on='unit_id', how='left', validate='many_to_one')
joined['day'] = pd.to_datetime(joined['time']).dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
print('rows', len(joined), 'unmatched source', joined['sample_key'].isna().sum(), 'unmatched design', joined['treatment'].isna().sum())
print('view/source date mismatches', joined['day'].ne(joined['date']).sum())
print('observed date range', joined['day'].min(), joined['day'].max())
window = joined.loc[joined['day'].between('2026-04-14', '2026-04-27')].copy()
positive = window['value'].gt(0)
inside = (
    window['feature_bbox_row_start_px'].gt(window['tray_roi_crop_row_start_px'])
    & window['feature_bbox_row_stop_px'].lt(window['tray_roi_crop_row_stop_px'])
    & window['feature_bbox_col_start_px'].gt(window['tray_roi_crop_col_start_px'])
    & window['feature_bbox_col_stop_px'].lt(window['tray_roi_crop_col_stop_px'])
)
print('window rows', len(window), 'positive', int(positive.sum()), 'positive and non-edge-contact', int((positive & inside).sum()))
valid = window.loc[positive & inside, ['unit_id', 'treatment', 'genotype', 'day', 'value']].copy()
plant_day = valid.groupby(['unit_id', 'treatment', 'genotype', 'day'], as_index=False)['value'].median()
summary = plant_day.groupby(['treatment', 'day']).agg(median_area_px=('value', 'median'), plants=('unit_id', 'nunique')).reset_index()
print('plant-day rows', len(plant_day))
for treatment in ['0', '50', '100', '200', '500', '1000']:
    group = summary.loc[summary['treatment'].eq(treatment)]
    print('treatment', treatment, 'days', len(group), 'n range', (group['plants'].min(), group['plants'].max()))
    print(group.loc[group['day'].isin(['2026-04-14', '2026-04-20', '2026-04-27'])].to_string(index=False))
base = plant_day.loc[plant_day['day'].eq('2026-04-14'), ['unit_id', 'value']].rename(columns={'value': 'baseline_px'})
end = plant_day.loc[plant_day['day'].eq('2026-04-27'), ['unit_id']]
cohort = base.merge(end, on='unit_id', validate='one_to_one')
paired = plant_day.merge(cohort, on='unit_id', how='inner', validate='many_to_one')
print('paired cohort by treatment', paired[['unit_id', 'treatment']].drop_duplicates().groupby('treatment').size().to_dict())
print('paired cohort plant-day coverage by treatment', paired.groupby(['treatment', 'day'])['unit_id'].nunique().groupby('treatment').agg(['min', 'max']).to_string())
'@ | uv run --no-project --with pandas --with pyarrow python -

@'
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
import pyarrow.parquet as pq


def main() -> None:
    """Plot matched-plant RGB2 growth curves with daily coverage."""
    workspace = Path(r'D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\opal-work\live\ws')
    bundle = Path(r'D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\OPAL\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC')
    views = workspace / '.clio' / 'datasets' / '76bf90275f7a9839' / 'views'
    observed = pq.read_table(
        views / 'observations_rgb2_features_000.parquet',
        columns=['unit_id', 'time', 'trait', 'value', 'source_row_key'],
    ).to_pandas()
    observed = observed.loc[observed['trait'].eq('area_px')].copy()
    bounds = [
        'tray_roi_crop_row_start_px', 'tray_roi_crop_row_stop_px',
        'tray_roi_crop_col_start_px', 'tray_roi_crop_col_stop_px',
        'feature_bbox_row_start_px', 'feature_bbox_row_stop_px',
        'feature_bbox_col_start_px', 'feature_bbox_col_stop_px',
    ]
    source = pq.read_table(
        bundle / 'rgb2' / 'rgb2-features.parquet',
        columns=['sample_key', *bounds],
    ).to_pandas()
    design = pq.read_table(
        views / 'design.parquet', columns=['unit_id', 'treatment']
    ).to_pandas()
    data = observed.merge(
        source, left_on='source_row_key', right_on='sample_key',
        how='left', validate='one_to_one',
    ).merge(design, on='unit_id', how='left', validate='many_to_one')
    if data['sample_key'].isna().any() or data['treatment'].isna().any():
        raise ValueError('RGB2 source or design join has unmatched rows')
    data['day'] = pd.to_datetime(data['time']).dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
    data = data.loc[data['day'].between('2026-04-14', '2026-04-27')].copy()
    inside = (
        data['feature_bbox_row_start_px'].gt(data['tray_roi_crop_row_start_px'])
        & data['feature_bbox_row_stop_px'].lt(data['tray_roi_crop_row_stop_px'])
        & data['feature_bbox_col_start_px'].gt(data['tray_roi_crop_col_start_px'])
        & data['feature_bbox_col_stop_px'].lt(data['tray_roi_crop_col_stop_px'])
    )
    valid = data.loc[data['value'].gt(0) & inside,
                     ['unit_id', 'treatment', 'day', 'value']]
    plant_day = valid.groupby(
        ['unit_id', 'treatment', 'day'], as_index=False
    )['value'].median()
    endpoints = plant_day.loc[
        plant_day['day'].isin(['2026-04-14', '2026-04-27'])
    ].groupby('unit_id')['day'].nunique()
    cohort_ids = endpoints.index[endpoints.eq(2)]
    paired = plant_day.loc[plant_day['unit_id'].isin(cohort_ids)].copy()
    summary = paired.groupby(['treatment', 'day'])['value'].agg(
        plants='count', median_area_px='median',
        p25_area_px=lambda values: values.quantile(0.25),
        p75_area_px=lambda values: values.quantile(0.75),
    ).reset_index()
    cohort_counts = paired[['unit_id', 'treatment']].drop_duplicates().groupby('treatment').size()
    csv_path = workspace / 'rgb2_growth_curves_apr14_27.csv'
    png_path = workspace / 'rgb2_growth_curves_apr14_27.png'
    summary.to_csv(csv_path, index=False)
    fig, (area_ax, count_ax) = plt.subplots(
        2, 1, figsize=(11, 8), sharex=True,
        gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [3, 1]},
    )
    for treatment in ['0', '50', '100', '200', '500', '1000']:
        group = summary.loc[summary['treatment'].eq(treatment)].sort_values('day')
        dates = pd.to_datetime(group['day'])
        line, = area_ax.plot(
            dates, group['median_area_px'], marker='o', markersize=3,
            linewidth=2, label=f'{treatment} (cohort n={cohort_counts[treatment]})',
        )
        area_ax.fill_between(
            dates, group['p25_area_px'], group['p75_area_px'],
            color=line.get_color(), alpha=0.10,
        )
        count_ax.plot(dates, group['plants'], color=line.get_color(), linewidth=1.5)
    area_ax.set_ylabel('Projected canopy area (pixels)')
    area_ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
    area_ax.grid(alpha=0.2)
    area_ax.legend(title='Treatment label', ncol=2, fontsize=9)
    count_ax.set_ylabel('Plants/day')
    count_ax.set_xlabel('2026 measurement date')
    count_ax.grid(alpha=0.2)
    fig.suptitle('RGB2 growth curves, April 14–27 (matched endpoint cohort)')
    fig.text(
        0.01, 0.01,
        'Lines: daily median across plants; shading: 25th–75th percentiles. '
        'Each plant-day uses its median positive, non-ROI-edge-contact area. '
        'Treatment labels are categorical; dose unit is unconfirmed.',
        fontsize=8,
    )
    fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.045, 1, 0.96])
    fig.savefig(png_path, dpi=180, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.close(fig)
    print(f'figure={png_path}')
    print(f'table={csv_path}')
    print(f'cohort_counts={cohort_counts.to_dict()}')
    print(f'daily_rows={len(summary)}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

Skill directory (use as SKILL_ROOT): D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\opal-work\clio-agent-chart-guidance\src\clio_agent\gact\builtin_skills\present-interactive-analysis
Use this generic presentation skill only after the underlying evidence exists and
only when interaction or structure helps the user more than prose. A2UI is a view
of observed state, never an analysis substitute. Do not mention the protocol or
ask the user to supply component payloads.

Component shapes are NOT in this skill — the catalog itself is the allowlist and
the source of truth (`docs/design/a2ui-compat-campaign-2026-09.md` S2/S4). Load a
catalog's index with `load_skill("a2ui-catalog-<slug>")` (see "Skills available to
you" for the ids your session can currently produce) and one component's exact
schema with `load_skill("a2ui-catalog-<slug>", file="catalog.json#/components/<Name>")`
before producing it.

## Choosing a view

Match the surface to the shape of the evidence, not to what looks impressive:

- A spatial result (stations, sites, points on a map) → a map component.
- Structured rows and columns → a data table.
- A quantity that changes over an index or time for a few series → an interactive
  time series.
- Many entities or grouped comparisons (one line per sample over time, spectra,
  distributions per group, a matrix of values) → the catalog's general chart
  component. Use one of its **named presets** by filling in field names; don't
  write a chart spec by hand unless no preset fits. That's longer, more likely to
  fail, and still has to pass the catalog's spec guard.
- For anything non-trivial in size, pass a registered artifact reference instead
  of inlined rows. Let the server-side query filter, aggregate or downsample it
  (for example, a bounded number of points per entity) instead of trimming the
  data yourself.
- A single observed value → one metric component per value.
- Ongoing/completed work, a warning, or a diff → the matching status/callout/diff
  component, never repurposing a generic text block for it.
- A durable export (an image, a report) the user did not ask to view inline → a
  registered artifact reference, not an inlined image.

## Composing surfaces

Prefer one small surface at the step it explains. Reuse a stable semantic
`surface_id` to update that view in place. Do not accumulate unrelated work into
one final tabbed dashboard. Tabs are appropriate only when several views of the
same result belong together and the available width justifies them.

## Custom charts with Altair

The general chart component renders **Vega-Lite**. When no named preset fits
(a layered overlay, a particular facet layout, a custom encoding), write the
chart in Python with **Altair**, which produces Vega-Lite, and pass the
exported spec to the component instead of writing Vega-Lite JSON by hand.

- **Data comes only from the component.** Build every chart on
  `alt.NamedData("source")`. A DataFrame, URL or inline values passed to
  `alt.Chart(...)` get inlined into the spec, and the server's chart guard
  refuses them. Rows arrive through the component's inline data or its
  artifact reference.
- **Shared selection.** Define one point selection whose name matches the
  component's selection parameter, over the entity field. The component's
  selection binding then links the chart to the other views (see below).
- **Keep specs small.** The guard caps size, nesting and view count. No URLs
  anywhere.

Write a Python file that assigns the Altair chart to `chart`, resolve this
skill's directory as `SKILL_ROOT`, and export plus pre-check it:

```text
uv run --no-project --with "altair>=5" python "SKILL_ROOT/scripts/vega_spec.py" build "CHART.py" "SPEC.json"
```

The script writes the spec and names any rule it would obviously break;
`vega_spec.py check SPEC.json` re-checks an existing spec. The server's guard
is the final authority. Load the chart component's schema from the catalog
skill before putting the spec into a surface.

## Linking views on one surface

To let several views on the same surface follow one selection, bind each view's
selection to the same data-model path under `/selection/`, one path per concept
(e.g. the selected samples). A chart, table or map on that surface then
highlights whatever the others select, entirely in the client, with no agent
turn. Use this whenever views show the same entities from different angles.
Views on different surfaces don't share selection.

## Preserving a user's choice into the next turn

A click or selection inside a surface is local visual state only — it does not by
itself reach the agent. When the user must choose among options before analysis
continues, pair the selector with a submit action whose event delivers the
resolved selection as structured context; load the catalog's Button/action and
your chosen selector's schemas together so the wiring between them is correct on
the first try.

## Producing and verifying

Call `create_a2ui_surface` once per coherent revision (leave `catalog_id` empty
to use the session's negotiated catalog). Require `rendered=true` and
`state=ready` before saying the view is available. A refusal names what to load
next (`hint`) — load exactly that component's schema, correct the call, and
retry a bounded number of times; do not print the payload as chat text, silently
replace an interactive component with a static image, or claim success on a
refusal.

import pandas as pd
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

workspace = Path(r'D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\opal-work\live\ws')
bundle = Path(r'D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\OPAL\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC')
views = workspace / '.clio' / 'datasets' / '76bf90275f7a9839' / 'views'

observed = pq.read_table(
    views / 'observations_rgb2_features_000.parquet',
    columns=['unit_id', 'time', 'trait', 'value', 'source_row_key'],
).to_pandas()
observed = observed.loc[observed['trait'].eq('area_px')].copy()
source_columns = [
    'sample_key', 'date',
    'tray_roi_crop_row_start_px', 'tray_roi_crop_row_stop_px',
    'tray_roi_crop_col_start_px', 'tray_roi_crop_col_stop_px',
    'feature_bbox_row_start_px', 'feature_bbox_row_stop_px',
    'feature_bbox_col_start_px', 'feature_bbox_col_stop_px',
]
source = pq.read_table(bundle / 'rgb2' / 'rgb2-features.parquet', columns=source_columns).to_pandas()
design = pq.read_table(views / 'design.parquet', columns=['unit_id', 'treatment', 'genotype']).to_pandas()
joined = observed.merge(source, left_on='source_row_key', right_on='sample_key', how='left', validate='one_to_one')
joined = joined.merge(design, on='unit_id', how='left', validate='many_to_one')
joined['day'] = pd.to_datetime(joined['time']).dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')

print('observed date range', joined['day'].min(), joined['day'].max())
window = joined.loc[joined['day'].between('2026-04-14', '2026-04-27')].copy()
positive = window['value'].gt(0)
inside = (
    window['feature_bbox_row_start_px'].gt(window['tray_roi_crop_row_start_px'])
    & window['feature_bbox_row_stop_px'].lt(window['tray_roi_crop_row_stop_px'])
    & window['feature_bbox_col_start_px'].gt(window['tray_roi_crop_col_start_px'])

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
import pyarrow.parquet as pq


def main() -> None:
    """Plot matched-plant RGB2 growth curves with daily coverage."""
    workspace = Path(r'D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\opal-work\live\ws')
    bundle = Path(r'D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\OPAL\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC')
    views = workspace / '.clio' / 'datasets' / '76bf90275f7a9839' / 'views'
    observed = pq.read_table(
        views / 'observations_rgb2_features_000.parquet',
        columns=['unit_id', 'time', 'trait', 'value', 'source_row_key'],
    ).to_pandas()
    observed = observed.loc[observed['trait'].eq('area_px')].copy()
    bounds = [
        'tray_roi_crop_row_start_px', 'tray_roi_crop_row_stop_px',
        'tray_roi_crop_col_start_px', 'tray_roi_crop_col_stop_px',
        'feature_bbox_row_start_px', 'feature_bbox_row_stop_px',
        'feature_bbox_col_start_px', 'feature_bbox_col_stop_px',
    ]
    source = pq.read_table(
        bundle / 'rgb2' / 'rgb2-features.parquet',
        columns=['sample_key', *bounds],
    ).to_pandas()
    design = pq.read_table(
        views / 'design.parquet', columns=['unit_id', 'treatment']
    ).to_pandas()
    data = observed.merge(
        source, left_on='source_row_key', right_on='sample_key',
        how='left', validate='one_to_one',
    ).merge(design, on='unit_id', how='left', validate='many_to_one')
    if data['sample_key'].isna().any() or data['treatment'].isna().any():
        raise ValueError('RGB2 source or design join has unmatched rows')
    data['day'] = pd.to_datetime(data['time']).dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
    data = data.loc[data['day'].between('2026-04-14', '2026-04-27')].copy()
    inside = (
        data['feature_bbox_row_start_px'].gt(data['tray_roi_crop_row_start_px'])
        & data['feature_bbox_row_stop_px'].lt(data['tray_roi_crop_row_stop_px'])
        & data['feature_bbox_col_start_px'].gt(data['tray_roi_crop_col_start_px'])
        & data['feature_bbox_col_stop_px'].lt(data['tray_roi_crop_col_stop_px'])
    )
    valid = data.loc[data['value'].gt(0) & inside,
                     ['unit_id', 'treatment', 'day', 'value']]
    plant_day = valid.groupby(
        ['unit_id', 'treatment', 'day'], as_index=False
    )['value'].median()
    endpoints = plant_day.loc[
        plant_day['day'].isin(['2026-04-14', '2026-04-27'])
    ].groupby('unit_id')['day'].nunique()
    cohort_ids = endpoints.index[endpoints.eq(2)]
    paired = plant_day.loc[plant_day['unit_id'].isin(cohort_ids)].copy()
    summary = paired.groupby(['treatment', 'day'])['value'].agg(
        plants='count', median_area_px='median',
        p25_area_px=lambda values: values.quantile(0.25),
        p75_area_px=lambda values: values.quantile(0.75),
    ).reset_index()
    cohort_counts = paired[['unit_id', 'treatment']].drop_duplicates().groupby('treatment').size()
    csv_path = workspace / 'rgb2_growth_curves_apr14_27.csv'
    png_path = workspace / 'rgb2_growth_curves_apr14_27.png'
    summary.to_csv(csv_path, index=False)
    fig, (area_ax, count_ax) = plt.subplots(
        2, 1, figsize=(11, 8), sharex=True,
        gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [3, 1]},
    )
    for treatment in ['0', '50', '100', '200', '500', '1000']:
        group = summary.loc[summary['treatment'].eq(treatment)].sort_values('day')
        dates = pd.to_datetime(group['day'])
        line, = area_ax.plot(
            dates, group['median_area_px'], marker='o', markersize=3,
            linewidth=2, label=f'{treatment} (cohort n={cohort_counts[treatment]})',
        )
        area_ax.fill_between(
            dates, group['p25_area_px'], group['p75_area_px'],
            color=line.get_color(), alpha=0.10,
        )
        count_ax.plot(dates, group['plants'], color=line.get_color(), linewidth=1.5)
    area_ax.set_ylabel('Projected canopy area (pixels)')
    area_ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
    area_ax.grid(alpha=0.2)
    area_ax.legend(title='Treatment label', ncol=2, fontsize=9)
    count_ax.set_ylabel('Plants/day')
    count_ax.set_xlabel('2026 measurement date')
    count_ax.grid(alpha=0.2)
    fig.suptitle('RGB2 growth curves, April 14–27 (matched endpoint cohort)')
    fig.text(
        0.01, 0.01,
        'Lines: daily median across plants; shading: 25th–75th percentiles. '
        'Each plant-day uses its median positive, non-ROI-edge-contact area. '
        'Treatment labels are categorical; dose unit is unconfirmed.',
        fontsize=8,
    )
    fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.045, 1, 0.96])
    fig.savefig(png_path, dpi=180, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.close(fig)
    print(f'figure={png_path}')
    print(f'table={csv_path}')
    print(f'cohort_counts={cohort_counts.to_dict()}')
    print(f'daily_rows={len(summary)}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

## Choosing a view

Match the surface to the shape of the evidence, not to what looks impressive:

- A spatial result (stations, sites, points on a map) → a map component.
- Structured rows and columns → a data table.
- A quantity that changes over an index or time for a few series → an interactive
  time series.
- Many entities or grouped comparisons (one line per sample over time, spectra,
  distributions per group, a matrix of values) → the catalog's general chart
  component. Use one of its **named presets** by filling in field names; don't
  write a chart spec by hand unless no preset fits. That's longer, more likely to
  fail, and still has to pass the catalog's spec guard.

  of inlined rows. Let the server-side query filter, aggregate or downsample it
  (for example, a bounded number of points per entity) instead of trimming the
  data yourself.

# Skill: size-and-growth-traits
Skill directory (use as SKILL_ROOT): D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\opal-work\live\ws\.clio\agent-blueprints\appl-core\skills\size-and-growth-traits
# Size and growth traits (draft)

Size traits come from segmentation masks (2D images) or surfaces/point clouds
(3D scans). They are proxies: projected area, height, volume-like products,
and pot weights all measure something related to, but not equal to, biomass.

## Checks before any comparison

1. **Scale.** Pixel values are only comparable within one camera setup. For
   any metric value, check the conversion: object size against the documented
   frame, container, or tray size; the same trait from another instrument
   (2D projected area vs a 3D scan's projected area). A disagreement by a
   large factor means the metric scale is suspect -- use pixels within a
   sensor, and ask the owners.
2. **Mask choice.** A trait computed on a different mask (vendor vs ML model,
   or different thresholds) is a different method. Check which mask each
   value used and do not mix them.
3. **Saturation and clipping.** For each session, compute the fraction of
   units whose bounding box touches the crop/frame edge, and the median trait
   over time. A plateau that coincides with edge contact or canopy overlap is
   a measurement limit. Truncate or flag growth curves from that point on.
4. **Empty masks.** Zero-coverage rows are missing values, not tiny plants.
5. **Weights.** Pot weight includes pot, substrate, and water; watering events
   dominate it. Do not read pot weight as plant mass without a documented
   tare and a watering model.
6. **Repeated sessions per day.** Size can differ between morning and evening
   sessions (leaf movement, turgor). Fix one session per day or average per
   day before fitting curves.

## Growth curves

- One curve per unit: trait vs time (days after sowing/treatment if known;
  otherwise days since first session, stated as such).
- Summaries: area under the curve, final size before any clipping onset,
  absolute and relative growth rate over a window (relative growth rate on
  log-scale values), time to reach a threshold.
- Fit smooth models (logistic, Gompertz, or splines) only on the unclipped
  part; report the window used.
- Compare groups with the repeated-measures methods in `treatment-response`,
  not with one t-test per day.

## Report

State units and their tag (stated/checked/inferred), the mask/method, the
session choice, the clipping cut-off, and how many units each curve group
contains.

Skill directory (use as SKILL_ROOT): D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\opal-work\live\ws\.clio\agent-blueprints\appl-core\skills\treatment-response
# Treatment response (draft)

## Decide the model from the design, not from the question

1. **What is the treatment?** Read the design view and the card. A numeric
   dose with a confirmed unit supports dose-response; a category (control vs
   treated, named agents) supports contrasts only. If the card lists the
   treatment's meaning as an open question, say the analysis treats levels as
   unordered categories and why.
2. **What is the unit of replication?** Usually the plant/pot. Several images
   of the same plant are repeated measures, not replicates. Count replicates
   per cell from `design`.
3. **What else structures the data?** Genotype, tray/position, block, session.
   If treatments are mixed within trays, position can be a covariate or random
   effect; if trays are confounded with treatment, say that effects cannot be
   separated.

## Methods

- **Categorical treatments**: compare per genotype and overall; with
  replicates per cell, use a two-way model (genotype, treatment, and their
  interaction); report effect sizes with intervals, not only p-values.
- **Doses**: fit a response curve per genotype (log-logistic for
  inhibition, or a monotone spline) when there are enough levels; report
  EC-style summaries only when the curve is identifiable within the tested
  range. With few levels, treat doses as ordered categories and test a trend.
- **Genotype x treatment**: test the interaction; rank genotypes by response
  (difference or ratio to their own control), not by raw means.
- **Repeated measures**: summarise each unit's trajectory first (area under
  curve, final unclipped value, growth rate -- see `size-and-growth-traits`),
  then compare the summaries; or fit a mixed model with unit as a random
  effect. Never pool all sessions as if independent.
- **Multiple testing**: correct across genotypes/traits (for example
  Benjamini-Hochberg) and say so.
- **Unbalanced cells**: use models that handle imbalance (type II/III sums of
  squares, mixed models); report the cell counts.

## Checks before reporting

- Outliers and scale errors removed per the card, with counts.
- Units and relative vs absolute scales stated; relative units (a.u.) are not
  compared across instruments.
- Every number comes from computed output (script or tool), with the model
  and the sample size.

# Evidence and claims

Every statement you make about a dataset carries one tag. The tag says how
the reader can check it.

| Tag | Meaning | Provenance line must name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[stated]` | The data's own documentation, manifest, or catalog says it | the file and section, or the manifest key |
| `[checked]` | You verified it in the data during this work | the command/script and the number it printed, or the card entry that recorded it |
| `[inferred]` | Your interpretation: plausible, not established by the files | the evidence it rests on, and who can confirm it |

Rules:

1. **Default to the weaker tag.** A column name is not documentation: a
   `_mm` suffix is `[stated]` only if a document defines it; that the values
   are millimetres is `[checked]` only after a plausibility check; that they
   are *correct* millimetres may still be `[inferred]`.
2. **`[stated]` is not `[checked]`.** Documentation can be wrong or stale.
   When a stated fact matters for a result (a unit, a count, a formula),
   check it and record both.
3. **Every `[inferred]` fact is also an open question** unless the user has
   confirmed it in this conversation (then record who confirmed it and
   re-tag it `[stated]` with the user as the source).
4. **Provenance lines are short and reproducible**: `(source: README,
   "Units" section)`, `(evidence: audit_columns.py on <table>, 12% empty)`,
   `(why: plateau coincides with bounding boxes at crop edge)`. Copy numbers
   from tool output; never round them into new facts.
5. **Numbers in answers come from the current tool output or the card**, with
   the tag of their source. If you did not compute it, do not state it.

## Open questions for data owners

Ask instead of guessing whenever the answer changes an analysis: what a
treatment or factor level means and its unit, whether a suspicious unit or
scale is real, whether zeros or blanks are real values, which of two
disagreeing sources is authoritative, what an undocumented flag means. Write
each as one question plus why it matters. In an interactive session, ask the
user (with `ask_user` when available) and continue with the conservative
choice meanwhile; in a child agent, only record the question.

## Reporting uncertainty

- Separate what is known from what is assumed in every answer: a short
  "Assumptions" or "Caveats" line is enough.
- State the scope of a check: sample vs full table, which tables, which
  period.
- Prefer ranges and counts with denominators ("in 412 of 2,000 sampled rows")
  over adjectives ("many").
- When evidence conflicts, show both sides and say which one the analysis
  used and why.
- A null result is a result: say what was checked and found clean.

## Open questions for data owners

- What substance or intervention do treatment labels `0`, `50`, `100`, `200`, `500`, and `1000` represent, and are they doses with a unit? This determines whether dose-response analysis is valid.
- What timezone, if any, applies to image, round, and weighing timestamps? This affects cross-sensor timing and daily aggregation.
- Are FC1 float64-maximum values vendor missing-value codes, and should `-99`/`9999` and feature-table `32767` also be treated as missing? This changes trait summaries.
- Are zero pre- or post-watering weights genuine observations or failed readings? This changes water/weight analyses.
- Which of the duplicate weight readings at the same plant and timestamp should be authoritative, if either? This changes longitudinal weight summaries.
- For FC1 variables available as both vendor scalars and masked parameter-image medians, which method is intended for each scientific comparison? This changes fluorescence results.
- Are S3D canonical metric units calibrated and comparable to other sensors, given the `a.u.` vendor-unit fields? This changes cross-sensor size comparisons.
- Should `Warning` and `UserTerminated` rounds be excluded, and how should multiple same-day sessions be selected or aggregated? This changes time-course analyses.
- Are the VNIR/SWIR reflectance values radiometrically calibrated and comparable between sessions, and which wavelength calibration should be considered authoritative? This changes spectral interpretation.
- Are RGB/MSC/VNIR/SWIR feature-name suffixes and undocumented indices sufficient to assign physical scales? The loader uses conservative name-derived scales where a documented unit is absent; interpretation needs confirmation.

## Proposed lessons

- check: whether a source-specific long table uses a different key format from its companion feature table before joining.
- check: whether empty wavelength columns coexist with populated columns bearing slightly different calibrated wavelength labels.
- check: whether duplicate plant–timestamp measurements have distinct source measurement IDs and disagree in value.
- check: whether a derived shape index becomes extreme exactly when its denominator-like perimeter is zero.

- What substance or intervention do treatment labels `0`, `50`, `100`, `200`, `500`, and `1000` represent, and are they doses with a unit? This determines whether dose-response analysis is valid.
- What timezone, if any, applies to image, round, and weighing timestamps? This affects cross-sensor timing and daily aggregation.
- Are FC1 float64-maximum values vendor missing-value codes, and should `-99`/`9999` and feature-table `32767` also be treated as missing? This changes trait summaries.
- Are zero pre- or post-watering weights genuine observations or failed readings? This changes water/weight analyses.
- Which of the duplicate weight readings at the same plant and timestamp should be authoritative, if either? This changes longitudinal weight summaries.
- For FC1 variables available as both vendor scalars and masked parameter-image medians, which method is intended for each scientific comparison? This changes fluorescence results.
- Are S3D canonical metric units calibrated and comparable to other sensors, given the `a.u.` vendor-unit fields? This changes cross-sensor size comparisons.
- Should `Warning` and `UserTerminated` rounds be excluded, and how should multiple same-day sessions be selected or aggregated? This changes time-course analyses.
- Are the VNIR/SWIR reflectance values radiometrically calibrated and comparable between sessions, and which wavelength calibration should be considered authoritative? This changes spectral interpretation.
- Are RGB/MSC/VNIR/SWIR feature-name suffixes and undocumented indices sufficient to assign physical scales? The loader uses conservative name-derived scales where a documented unit is absent; interpretation needs confirmation.

input.command: uv run --with pyarrow python -c "import collections, math, statistics; import pyarrow.parquet as pq; p=r'D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\opal-work\live\ws\.clio\datasets\76bf90275f7a9839\views\observations_s3d_plant.parquet'; d=pq.read_table(p,columns=['unit_id','time','trait','value','qc']).to_pydict(); rows=[(u,t,v,q) for u,t,tr,v,q in zip(d['unit_id'],d['time'],d['trait'],d['value'],d['qc']) if tr=='projected_area_mm2']; valid=[(u,t,v,q) for u,t,v,q in rows if v is not None and math.isfinite(v) and v>0]; print('rows',len(rows),'plants',len(set(u for u,t,v,q in rows)),'valid_positive',len(valid)); print('qc',collections.Counter(str(q) for u,t,v,q in rows)); print('null',sum(v is None for u,t,v,q in rows),'zero_or_negative',sum(v is not None and math.isfinite(v) and v<=0 for u,t,v,q in rows)); print('dates',sorted(collections.Counter(str(t)[:10] for u,t,v,q in rows).items())); print('valid_range',min(v for u,t,v,q in valid),max(v for u,t,v,q in valid)); print('examples',rows[:5])"

**Preparing source values**

S3D projected-area measurements cover different numbers of plants on different dates, so an unadjusted overall mean could be misleading. I’ll check plant-level coverage and median area by treatment label on each date, then choose a comparison window that accounts for genotype and repeated measurements. I’ll exclude the five nonpositive area readings as unusable for growth.

@'
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from math import isfinite
from pathlib import Path
from statistics import median
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

root = Path(r'D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\opal-work\live\ws\.clio\datasets\76bf90275f7a9839\views')
design = pq.read_table(root / 'design.parquet', columns=['unit_id', 'genotype', 'treatment']).to_pylist()
assignments = {row['unit_id']: (row['genotype'], row['treatment']) for row in design}
observations = pq.read_table(root / 'observations_s3d_plant.parquet', columns=['unit_id', 'time', 'trait', 'value']).to_pylist()
by_plant_day = defaultdict(list)
unmatched = 0
for row in observations:
    if row['trait'] != 'projected_area_mm2':
        continue
    value = row['value']
    if value is None or not isfinite(value) or value <= 0:
        continue
    assignment = assignments.get(row['unit_id'])
    if assignment is None:
        unmatched += 1
        continue
    by_plant_day[(row['time'][:10], assignment[1], row['unit_id'])].append(value)
by_group_day = defaultdict(list)
for (day, treatment, unit_id), values in by_plant_day.items():
    by_group_day[(day, treatment)].append(median(values))
levels = ['0', '50', '100', '200', '500', '1000']
print('design plants by treatment:', dict(Counter(row['treatment'] for row in design)))
print('unmatched valid observations:', unmatched)
print('Each cell is distinct plants:median projected area (exported mm2); repeated same-day measurements are collapsed per plant.')
print('date | ' + ' | '.join(levels))
for day in sorted({key[0] for key in by_group_day}):
    cells = []
    for level in levels:
        values = by_group_day.get((day, level), [])
        cells.append(f'{len(values)}:{median(values):.1f}' if values else '0:NA')
    print(day + ' | ' + ' | '.join(cells))
'@ | uv run --with pyarrow python -

# RGB2 CLI Modality Report

```yaml
document_id: appl-core-cli-modality-rgb2
current_as_of: "2026-08-07"
modality_id: RGB2
title: "Top-view RGB imaging"
modality_kind: image
pipeline_status: implemented_pipeline
data_description: "Top-view RGB plant images with masked projected area, color, hue-bin, and vegetation color summaries."
source_systems:
  - PlantScreen RGB image records
  - APPL-CORE metadata manifest records
  - source RGB image files
spatial_context: "Top-view RGB frame, plant/tray assignment, tray ROI where available, fixed image/mask shape 3006 x 4104."
temporal_context: "RGB image datetime and round identity from metadata sync."
artifact_outputs:
  normalized_image: "images/exp_<experiment_id>/RGB2/<experiment_id>__<plant_id>__<round_id>.npy"
  appl_mask: "appl-masks/exp_<experiment_id>/RGB2/<experiment_id>__<plant_id>__<round_id>.npy"
  vit_mask: "vit-masks/exp_<experiment_id>/RGB2/<experiment_id>__<plant_id>__<round_id>.npy"
  feature_table: "features/parquet/RGB2/features.parquet"
export_outputs:
  - rgb2/rgb2-features.csv
  - rgb2/rgb2-features.parquet
  - rgb2/rgb2-metadata.csv
  - rgb2/rgb2-metadata.parquet
  - rgb2/rgb2-design.csv
  - rgb2/rgb2-design.parquet
  - rgb2/rgb2-columns.csv
  - rgb2/rgb2-columns.json
feature_outputs:
  shape_px: true
  shape_mm: true
  total_height: false
  color_medians_and_means: true
  hue_bins: 25
  vegetation_color_indices:
    - ngrdi_mean
    - proportional_red_mean
    - proportional_green_mean
    - proportional_blue_mean
  mask_coverage: true
standards_crosswalk:
  dublin_core: [identifier, description, source, date, coverage, format, relation]
  fgdc_csdgm: [Identification_Information, Data_Quality_Information, Entity_and_Attribute_Information]
  iso_19115_19139: [MD_Metadata, identificationInfo, dataQualityInfo, spatialRepresentationInfo, contentInfo]
```

## Scope And Biological Meaning

`RGB2` is the implemented top-view visible-light modality. For biologists, it describes canopy projected area, top-view shape, and color. It is often useful for growth tracking because top-view projected area can approximate canopy expansion.

## Current APPL-CORE Implementation

`RGB2` is a full pipeline modality and is eligible for VIT segmentation. Ingest opens the source image with Pillow, converts it to RGB, and writes a normalized NumPy array with expected shape `[3006, 4104, 3]`.

Feature extraction can use APPL or VIT masks. RGB2 millimeter traits use a hard-coded top-view pixel-to-millimeter scale in the feature code. Unlike RGB1, RGB2 does not export total height traits.

## Artifacts And Processing

Artifacts follow the standard pattern for image, APPL mask, VIT mask, and feature parquet outputs. The feature stage summarizes top-view mask geometry and color traits over masked pixels. Experiment export writes RGB2 feature, metadata, design, and column tables when feature rows exist.

## Metadata Inventory

Minimum metadata for `RGB2` should include:

- Description: top-view RGB image and projected canopy shape/color traits.
- Source: RGB image ID, source image role/path in internal metadata, source manifest record, APPL-CORE processing lineage, and selected mask source.
- Spatial context: plant/tray IDs, tray profile/type/area, image shape, mask shape, ROI crop, feature bounding box, top-view role, and fixed pixel-to-mm scale.
- Temporal context: acquisition datetime, date, time, round ID, round order, and protocol window.
- Technical context: RGB conversion, APPL/VIT mask source, hard-coded scaling, source image dimensions and normalized tray ROI context persisted by feature build, mask coverage, and QC flags.

from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

path = Path(r'D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\OPAL\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC\rgb2\rgb2-features.parquet')
schema = pq.read_schema(path)
print('Relevant fields:')
for name in schema.names:
    if any(term in name.lower() for term in ('mask', 'bbox', 'image', 'roi', 'qc', 'plant', 'round', 'sample', 'source')):

print('Rows:', len(rows))
print('Mask-path presence:', dict(Counter((bool(row.get('vit_mask_path')), bool(row.get('appl_mask_path'))) for row in rows)))

for row in rows[:5]:

@'
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from math import isfinite
from pathlib import Path
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

path = Path(r'D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\OPAL\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC\rgb2\rgb2-features.parquet')
schema = pq.read_schema(path)
print('Mask/provenance columns:', [name for name in schema.names if any(term in name.lower() for term in ('mask', 'segment', 'source', 'method'))])
columns = ['image_timestamp', 'qc_flags', 'area_px', 'feature_bbox_row_start_px', 'feature_bbox_row_stop_px', 'feature_bbox_col_start_px', 'feature_bbox_col_stop_px', 'tray_roi_crop_row_start_px', 'tray_roi_crop_row_stop_px', 'tray_roi_crop_col_start_px', 'tray_roi_crop_col_stop_px']
rows = pq.read_table(path, columns=columns).to_pylist()
by_day = defaultdict(Counter)
examples = []
for row in rows:
    day = row['image_timestamp'][:10]
    counts = by_day[day]
    counts['total'] += 1
    flags = row['qc_flags'] or []
    if 'low_mask_coverage' in flags:
        counts['low_coverage'] += 1
    if 'empty_mask' in flags:
        counts['empty_mask'] += 1
    area = row['area_px']
    if area is None or not isfinite(area) or area <= 0:
        continue
    counts['positive_area'] += 1
    bounds = [row['feature_bbox_row_start_px'], row['feature_bbox_row_stop_px'], row['feature_bbox_col_start_px'], row['feature_bbox_col_stop_px'], row['tray_roi_crop_row_start_px'], row['tray_roi_crop_row_stop_px'], row['tray_roi_crop_col_start_px'], row['tray_roi_crop_col_stop_px']]
    if all(value is not None for value in bounds):
        if len(examples) < 3:
            examples.append((day, area, bounds))
        if bounds[0] <= bounds[4] or bounds[1] >= bounds[5] or bounds[2] <= bounds[6] or bounds[3] >= bounds[7]:
            counts['bbox_touches_roi'] += 1
print('Positive-area examples (date, area_px, bbox then ROI bounds):', examples)
print('date | total | positive_area | low_coverage | empty_mask | bbox_touches_roi')
for day, counts in sorted(by_day.items()):
    print(day, counts['total'], counts['positive_area'], counts['low_coverage'], counts['empty_mask'], counts['bbox_touches_roi'], sep=' | ')
'@ | uv run --with pyarrow python -

@'
from collections import defaultdict
from math import isfinite
from pathlib import Path
from statistics import median
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

views = Path(r'D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\opal-work\live\ws\.clio\datasets\76bf90275f7a9839\views')
raw = Path(r'D:\Libraries\Documents\projects\OPAL\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC\67_2026.04.09_OPAL.0002_Weston_PC\rgb2\rgb2-features.parquet')
design = {row['unit_id']: (row['genotype'], row['treatment']) for row in pq.read_table(views / 'design.parquet', columns=['unit_id', 'genotype', 'treatment']).to_pylist()}
edge = {}
for row in pq.read_table(raw, columns=['sample_key', 'feature_bbox_row_start_px', 'feature_bbox_row_stop_px', 'feature_bbox_col_start_px', 'feature_bbox_col_stop_px', 'tray_roi_crop_row_start_px', 'tray_roi_crop_row_stop_px', 'tray_roi_crop_col_start_px', 'tray_roi_crop_col_stop_px']).to_pylist():
    bounds = [row[name] for name in ('feature_bbox_row_start_px', 'feature_bbox_row_stop_px', 'feature_bbox_col_start_px', 'feature_bbox_col_stop_px', 'tray_roi_crop_row_start_px', 'tray_roi_crop_row_stop_px', 'tray_roi_crop_col_start_px', 'tray_roi_crop_col_stop_px')]
    edge[row['sample_key']] = None if any(value is None for value in bounds) else (bounds[0] <= bounds[4] or bounds[1] >= bounds[5] or bounds[2] <= bounds[6] or bounds[3] >= bounds[7])
plant_day = defaultdict(list)
missing_source = 0
positive_rows = 0
excluded_edge = 0
examples = []
for path in sorted(views.glob('observations_rgb2_features_*.parquet')):
    for row in pq.read_table(path, columns=['unit_id', 'time', 'trait', 'value', 'source_row_key']).to_pylist():
        if row['trait'] != 'area_px' or row['value'] is None or not isfinite(row['value']) or row['value'] <= 0:
            continue
        positive_rows += 1
        if len(examples) < 3:
            examples.append((row['source_row_key'], row['unit_id'], row['time'], row['value']))
        clip = edge.get(row['source_row_key'])
        if clip is None:
            missing_source += 1
            continue
        if clip:
            excluded_edge += 1
            continue
        day = row['time'][:10]
        if '2026-04-14' <= day <= '2026-04-27' and row['unit_id'] in design:
            plant_day[(row['unit_id'], day)].append(row['value'])
plant_daily = {(unit, day): median(values) for (unit, day), values in plant_day.items()}
print('examples:', examples)
print('positive_rows:', positive_rows, 'missing_source_or_bounds:', missing_source, 'excluded_edge:', excluded_edge)
levels = ['0', '50', '100', '200', '500', '1000']
print('date | ' + ' | '.join(levels) + ' (distinct plants:median area_px)')
for day in sorted({day for unit, day in plant_daily}):
    cells = []
    for level in levels:
        values = [value for (unit, current_day), value in plant_daily.items() if current_day == day and design[unit][1] == level]
        cells.append(f'{len(values)}:{median(values):.1f}' if values else '0:NA')
    print(day + ' | ' + ' | '.join(cells))
start, end = '2026-04-14', '2026-04-27'
print('Paired plant changes, April 14 to April 27; one median per plant per day:')
for level in levels:
    pairs = [(plant_daily[(unit, start)], plant_daily[(unit, end)]) for unit, (genotype, treatment) in design.items() if treatment == level and (unit, start) in plant_daily and (unit, end) in plant_daily]
    if pairs:
        print(level, 'n=', len(pairs), 'median_start=', median(a for a, b in pairs), 'median_end=', median(b for a, b in pairs), 'median_change=', median(b-a for a, b in pairs), 'median_ratio=', median(b/a for a, b in pairs))
'@ | uv run --with pyarrow python -
